1.where_you_see_it: At any vegetable market, brinjals of the same kind differ in size, shape and shade of purple: no two are exactly alike. That natural variation, partly inherited, is what farmers have always chosen their seed from.
1.picture: A 17-year-old school boy at a Tamil Nadu vegetable market, looking at a heap of purple brinjals that vary naturally in size, shape and shade. The heap of brinjals is the large, clear focus, seen close up. Simple market stall background, daylight.

4.hook: How can a breeder tell whether a tall plant will pass on only tallness to all its seeds?
4.link: A tall plant can be TT (true-breeding) or Tt (carrying the hidden dwarf allele). In a test cross it is crossed with a dwarf (tt) plant: if all offspring are tall it was TT; if half are dwarf it was Tt. The hidden allele is revealed by its offspring.
4.beyond_school: Seed farms and plant breeders use test crosses to confirm that a parent plant is true-breeding before its seed is multiplied and sold. This is why certified seed grows into the variety written on the packet.
4.picture: A 17-year-old school girl walks with a farmer along a seed farm plot of healthy green paddy plants in Tamil Nadu, both looking at the plants. The paddy plants are the large, clear focus. Simple field background, clear daylight.

7.hook: Why can a red and a white four o'clock flower give pink offspring?
7.link: In incomplete dominance neither allele fully hides the other: crossing a red (R1R1) and a white (R2R2) four o'clock plant gives pink (R1R2) offspring, an in-between colour. In codominance, both alleles show fully side by side instead, as in the AB blood group.
7.where_you_see_it: The four o'clock plant (andhi mandharai) that opens its flowers every evening near many Tamil Nadu homes comes in red, white and pink. The pink ones show how a red and a white parent can give an in-between colour.
7.beyond_school: Blood banks test blood groups before every transfusion. In the AB group, both the A and B antigens appear on red blood cells (codominance), and identifying this correctly is part of what makes a transfusion safe.
7.picture: A 17-year-old school boy in a home garden in the evening, looking closely at a four o'clock plant with pink flowers. The pink flowers are the large, clear focus, seen close up. Plain background, soft evening light.

10.hook: Why aren't people simply 'tall' or 'short', but every height in between?
10.link: Some traits are controlled by many genes, each adding a small effect: polygenic inheritance. In wheat, kernel colour from three gene pairs gives seven shades from white to dark red. Human height works the same way, with food and health adding to it, so heights form a smooth range.
10.where_you_see_it: Look along your class line at morning assembly: there is no gap between 'tall' and 'short', just a smooth range of heights.
10.beyond_school: Plant and animal breeders improving grain yield, fruit size or milk yield work with polygenic traits. Because each gene adds only a little, they select patiently over many generations.
10.picture: A line of school students, boys and girls of about 17, standing in a row at morning assembly on a school ground. Heights are clearly mixed across boys and girls: the tallest student in the line is a girl, and boys and girls of every height stand side by side. Plain sky behind them, no text or boards.

11.hook: Why do farmers buy fresh hybrid paddy seed every season instead of saving their own?
11.link: Hybrid paddy seed is produced using cytoplasmic male sterility: a plant with S cytoplasm and rfrf nuclear genes makes no fertile pollen, so it cannot pollinate itself and must be crossed with a chosen male parent. Seed saved from the hybrid crop does not breed true, so farmers buy fresh hybrid seed.
11.beyond_school: Hybrid rice and maize seed is produced on a large scale using cytoplasmic male sterility. Without it, workers would have to remove the anthers from millions of flowers by hand; CMS makes hybrid seed production practical and affordable for farmers.
11.picture: A 17-year-old school boy stands beside a farmer at a small paddy seed shop in a Tamil Nadu town. The farmer picks up a sealed paddy seed packet from a shelf of similar packets with simple labels. Close view of the two people and the packets against a plain shop wall.
